contributions.anchor: the p2 Summary Page's 'Contributions Received' — 'This Period' column (30,463.42), which is also the filer's own restatement of it two lines lower as 'Total Contributions Received' (30,463.42) and the printed grand total under the p3 'Contributions Received' ledger itself (30,463.42)
contributions.detail: 29 ledger rows sum to exactly 30,463.42 = the ledger's own printed grand total = the summary page's PER-PERIOD 'This Period' cell = its 'Total Contributions Received' line = its 'Subtotal' line. The 'Year to Date' column also prints 30,463.42 and was NOT summed as an increment — this is the cycle's FIRST report ('Seven days preceding the Primary Election'), so period IS year-to-date. NINE of the 29 rows are 'Kim Jackson Loan' (28,028.42 of the 30,463.42); they ARE itemized contribution rows because the ledger total that includes them is what the summary's contribution cell restates, and the beginning balance is nil so no line-3 slot exists for them (§B3, the Kirk/Grierson branch). The remaining 20 rows are 2,435.00 from outside donors. The balance ladder closes independently: nil + 30,463.42 − 27,007.61 = 3,455.81 = the printed 'Balance at Close of Reporting Period'. The one-past control rendered '$ 30,463.42' — that is the ledger's own printed SUM line (it sits below the Excel total rule and equals the stated total), NOT a §F1 trap-5 extra row.

in_kind_convention: monetary-only closed. The filer's own typed ledgers have no in-kind column, no in-kind line and no in-kind annotation on any row, and the summary page states a single undivided contributions figure with no separate in-kind line, so the monetary-only and monetary-plus-in-kind conventions give the identical sums (30,463.42 and 27,007.61). Both were tested; neither distinguishes.
escalation_note: No escalation was needed: pp2–4 are BORN-TYPED (an Excel print-out reproduced cleanly by the scan), every figure resolved unambiguously at the 200 dpi full-page read, and both sides close to the cent against three printed anchors each. 3.measure_note: ⚠ THIS PAGE IS NOT THE COUNTY FORM. It is the filer's own typed PORTRAIT ledger substituted for the county's Schedule A (ADDENDUM E §E5), so rowbands.py returns ZERO printed rules on it (h_rules_pct [], data_bands_pct [], skew +0.8) and the §6 underline-grid method is inapplicable. RECOVERY per §A2: `rowbands.py <pdf> 3 --text-lines --col 79,92` restricted to the amount column, which returns 31 text bands = the printed 'Amount' column HEADER (14.83–15.51) + 29 DATA ROWS + the ledger's own printed grand total (67.52–68.47). The 29 middle bands are stored here, one per printed ledger row, and are TIGHT GLYPH BANDS measured inside the amount column itself — which is what makes them valid despite the +0.8° skew (a band measured in one column does not transfer across a skewed sheet, so nothing here is extrapolated sideways). `cells` are read off the four printed header underlines from the render and are APPROXIMATE provenance only; `cell` (the amount column) is the one band proved by crop. PROOF CROPS at 1200 dpi and what they ACTUALLY RENDERED: (first row) pct:79.5,16.65,12.0,0.91@p3 --value rendered '$ 750.00' — the recorded row 1, and it also proves the filer did not start below the header. (last row) pct:79.5,65.47,12.0,0.95@p3 --value rendered '$ 1,673.42' with the Excel sum rule beneath it — the recorded row 29. (§B5 one-past control) pct:79.5,67.52,12.0,0.95@p3 --value rendered '$ 30,463.42'. Per §F1 a figure in the one-past band means EITHER trap 5 or the printed total; it is the printed total here, identified by the sum rule above it and by its equalling the summary page's stated figure to the cent — adding it as a 30th row would double the ledger.
